Methodology and data guide

Read the indicators with context.

This guide explains the complete career data and the limits of citation-based comparison.

On this pageCoverageIndicatorsInterpretationImplementation
Citation indicators describe patterns in publication and citation data. They are not a complete measure of scientific quality, contribution, or social value.

Coverage and editions

The website contains 1,541,862 usable annual records from career datasets released between 2019 and 2026. For 2021, the November revision is treated as the canonical edition. Release year and metric year are displayed separately.

The source methodology includes scientists who are among the top 100,000 by composite citation score or within the top 2% of their main subfield. Career-long and single-year datasets describe different periods; this website currently uses the career-long files.

Core indicators

  • Global rank orders records across the complete release.
  • Subfield rank compares scientists within the assigned subfield.
  • h-index combines publication volume and citation reach.
  • hm-index adjusts the h-index for co-authorship.
  • c-score is a composite citation indicator built from several measures.
  • Self-citation variants compare ranks and scores with self-citations included or excluded.

Responsible comparison

Raw ranks become harder to compare as the database grows. Release totals and shares provide context. Institution names are combined when differences are limited to capitalization, accents, punctuation, spacing, or a leading “The”. Abbreviations, renamed institutions, faculties, and other materially different affiliations remain separate until a reviewed authority file is available.

Institution and country counts describe representation among listed scientists. Without a suitable staff-size denominator, they should not be interpreted as performance rankings.

Some source records use the generic affiliation “College of Engineering” without naming a parent university. When a confidently linked scientist profile has a previous named affiliation, the website derives a separate engineering-college label, such as “Cornell University College of Engineering” or “UW College of Engineering”, and marks the annual affiliation as recovered. It does not add those records to the parent university. Unresolved generic records remain in the scientist data but are excluded from institution counts and rankings.

Static data architecture

The site is made of standard HTML pages. The complete data is split into gzip-compressed ranking pages, name-search indexes, institution and country histories, and hashed scientist-profile shards. Browsers fetch only the files required for the current view, which keeps the project suitable for GitHub and static hosting.
